λαασ.g: λᾶας , λᾶος, dat. λᾶι, acc. λᾶαν, du. λᾶε, pl. gen. λάων, dat. λάεσσι: stone.

λαγχανω.g: λαγχάνω , aor. ἔλαχον, λάχεν, redupl. subj. λελάχητε, perf. λέλογχεν: obtain by lot or by destiny, obtain, receive; abs., Il. 7.171; reversing the usual relation, Κὴρ λάχε γεινόμενον, ‘won me to her power at my birth,’ Il. 23.79; w. part. gen., Il. 24.76, Od. 5.311; causative, ‘put in possession of,’ ‘honor with,’ θανόντα πυρός, only with redupl. aor., *h 80, etc.; intrans., ‘fall by lot,’ Od. 9.160.

λαερκησ.g: Λαέρκης : (1) son of Aemon, father of Alcimedon, a Myrmidon, Il. 16.197.— (2) a goldsmith in Pylos, Od. 3.425.

λα_ερτησ.g: Λα_έρτης : Laertes, son of Arcīsius, and father of Odysseus, king in Ithaca, Od. 1.430, Od. 24.206, 270, Od. 4.111, 555, χ 185, Od. 24.219 ff.

λαζομαι.g: λάζομαι (=λαμβάνω), opt. 3 pl. λαζοίατο, ipf. (ἐ）λάζετο: take; γαῖαν ὀδάξ, ‘bite the dust,’ Il. 2.418 ; μῦθον πάλιν, ‘caught back again’ the words (of joy which were on his lips), Od. 13.254.

λαθι-κηδησ.g: λαθι-κηδής , ές (κῆδος): causing to forget care, ‘banishing care,’ Il. 22.83†.

λαθρη.g: λάθρῃ : secretly, unbeknown, τινός, ‘to one’; ‘imperceptibly,’ Il. 19.165.

λαιλαψ.g: λαῖλαψ , απος: tempest of wind and rain, hurricane.

λα_ινεοσ.g: λα_ΐνεος and λα?ϊνος (λᾶας): of stone, stony; τεῖχος, in the interpolated passage, Il. 12.177.

λαισηιον.g: λαισήιον : light shield or target; λαισήια πτερόεντα, perhaps so called on account of the ‘fluttering’ apron of untanned leather (λάσιος) hanging from the shield. (See adjoining cut and esp. No. 79.)

λαιστρυ_γων.g: Λαιστρυ_γών , pl. Λαιστρυ_γόνες: Laestrȳgon, the Laestrȳgons, a tribe of savage giants, Od. 10.106, 119, 199.

λαιτμα.g: λαῖτμα : the great gulf or abyss of the sea, usually w. ἁλός or θαλάσσης. (Od. and Il. 19.267.)

λαιφοσ.g: λαῖφος , εος: shabby, tattered garment, Od. 13.399 and Od. 20.206.

λαιψηροσ.g: λαιψηρός : nimble, swift; adv., λαιψηρὰ ἐνώμα_, ‘plied nimbly,’ Il. 15.269.

λακεδαιμων.g: Λακεδαίμων : Lacedaemon, the district whose capital was Sparta; epithets, δῖα, Od. 3.326; ἐρατεινή, Il. 3.239; εὐρύχορος, Od. 13.414; κοίλη, κητώεσσα, Od. 4.1.

λακτιζω.g: λακτίζω : kick with the heel, of the mortally wounded, struggling convulsively, Od. 18.99 and Od. 22.88.

λαμβανω.g: λαμβάνω , only aor. 2 act. and mid., ἔλλαβ（ε), ἐλλάβετ（ο), inf. redupl. λελαβέσθαι: take, receive, mid., take hold of; freq. w. part. gen.; sometimes of ‘seizing,’ ‘taking captive,’ Od. 11.4, Il. 11.114; in friendly sense, ‘take in,’ Od. 7.255; met., of feelings, χόλος, πένθος, τρόμος, etc.

λαμοσ.g: Λάμος : the king of the Laestrȳgons, Od. 10.81†.

λαμπετιδησ.g: Λαμπετίδης : son of Lampus, Dolops, Il. 15.526†.

λαμπετιη.g: Λαμπετίη : a nymph, daughter of Helius, Od. 12.132, 375.

λαμποσ.g: Λάμπος : (1) son of Laomedon, father of the Trojan Dolops, Il. 3.147, Il. 15.526.—(2) name of one of the steeds of Eos, Od. 23.246.—(3) one of Hector's horses, Il. 8.185.

λαμπροσ.g: λαμπρός , sup. λαμπρότατος: bright, brilliant, shining. (Il. and Od. 19.234.)

λαμπτηρ.g: λαμπτήρ , ῆρος: fire - pan, lightstand, cresset, to hold blazing pine splinters for illuminating, Od. 18.307, Od. 19.63. (See cuts, after bronze originals from Pompeii.)

λαμπω.g: λάμπω , ipf. ἔλαμπ（ε), λάμφ̓: shine, gleam, be radiant or brilliant.

λανθανω, ληθω.g: λανθάνω, λήθω , ipf. (ἐ）λάνθανον, ἔληθον, λῆθεν, iter. λήθεσκε, fut. λήσω, aor. 2 ἔλαθον, λάθον, subj. redupl. λε- λάθῃ, mid. λήθομαι, ipf. λανθανόμην, aor. 2 λάθετο, redupl. λελάθοντο, opt. 3 pl. λαθοίατο, imp. redupl. λελαθέσθω, perf. λέλασται, part. λελασμένος: I. act., escape the notice of, τινά, the obj. of the Greek verb usually appearing as the subj. in Eng., οὐδέ σε λήθω, ‘nor dost thou ever fail to mark me,’ Il. 1.561, Od. 17.305; the thing that one does when somebody else fails to mark him is regularly expressed by the part., ἄλλον πού τινα μᾶλλον Ἀχαιῶν χαλκοχιτώνων | λήθω μαρνάμενος, σὲ δὲ ϝιδμεναι αὐτὸν ὀίω, ‘another perchance is likely enough to overlook my prowess, but you know it right well,’ Il. 13.272. The learner cannot afford to be careless about the above meaning and construction. Sometimes w. ὅτι or ὅπως, ὅτε, Il. 17.626. The redupl. aor. is causative, make to forget; τινά τινος, Il. 15.60.—II. mid., forget; τινός, Δ 127, Od. 3.224.

λαξ.g: λάξ : adv., with the heel, with ποδί, Il. 10.158 and Od. 15.45.

λαο-γονοσ.g: Λαό-γονος : (1) a Trojan, the son of Onētor, slain by Meriones, Il. 16.604. —(2) a Trojan, the son of Bias, slain by Achilles, Il. 20.460.

λα_οδαμασ.g: Λα_όδαμας : (1) son of Antēnor, slain by Ajax, Il. 15.516.—(2) a Phaeacian, son of Alcinous, Od. 8.119, 132, η 170, Od. 8.117, 141.

λα_οδαμεια.g: Λα_οδάμεια : daughter of Bellerophon, and mother of Sarpēdon, Il. 6.198.

λα_οδικη.g: Λα_οδίκη : Laodice.—(1) a daughter of Agamemnon, Il. 9.145, 287.—(2) a daughter of Priam, wife of Helicāon, Il. 3.124, Il. 6.252.

λα_οδοκοσ.g: Λα_όδοκος : (1) a son of Antēnor, Il. 4.87.—(2) a comrade of Antilochus, Il. 17.699.

λαοθοη.g: Λαοθόη : daughter of Altes, mother of Lycāon, Il. 21.85, Il. 22.48.

λα_ομεδοντιαδησ.g: Λα_ομεδοντιάδης : son or descendant of Laomedon.—(1) Priam, Il. 3.250.—(2) Lampus, Il. 15.527.

λα_ομεδων.g: Λα_ομέδων : Laomedon, son of Ilus and father of Priam. He had promised his daughter Hesione to Heracles, on condition of her being delivered from the sea-monster sent by Poseidon to ravage the Troad, but proving false to his agreement was slain by Heracles, Il. 5.638 ff., 269, Il. 6.23, Il. 20.237, Il. 21.443.

λα_οσ.g: λα_ός , pl. λα_οί: people, host, esp. army; sometimes crew, crews, Od. 14.248; oftener the pl. than the sing., Il. 4.199, Il. 5.573.

λα_ο-σσοοσ.g: λα_ο-σσόος (σεύω): driving the people on (to combat), rousing the people; epith. of Ares, Eris, Athēne (Apollo, Amphiarāus), Il. 13.128, Od. 22.210.

λα_ο - φοροσ.g: λα_ο - φόρος : ὁδός, public way, Il. 15.682†.

λαπαρη.g: λαπάρη : the soft part of the body between hips and ribs, flank, loins. (Il.)

λαπιθαι.g: Λαπίθαι : the Lapithae, a warlike tribe dwelling by Mts. Olympus and Pelion in Thessaly, Il. 12.128, 181, Od. 21.297.

λαπτω.g: λάπτω , fut. part. λάψοντες: lap up with the tongue, Il. 16.161†.

λαρι_σα.g: Λάρι_σα : a town in Asia Minor, near Cyme, Il. 2.841, Il. 17.301.

λαρναξ.g: λάρναξ , ακος: chest, Il. 18.413; vase or urn, Il. 24.795.

λαροσ.g: λάρος : a sea bird, cormorant, with ὄρνι_ς, Od. 5.51†.

λα_ροσ.g: λα_ρός , sup. λα_ρώτατος: rich, fine, well-relished, Il. 17.572.

λασιοσ.g: λάσιος : hairy, shaggy, epith. of στῆθος, also κῆρ, as sign of manly strength and spirit; of sheep, wolly, Od. 9.433.

λασκω.g: λάσκω , aor. 2 λάκε, perf. part. w. pres. signif. λεληκώς, λελακυῖα: give voice, of animals, Scylla (as dog), a falcon, Il. 22.141; of things, sound, χαλκός, ἀσπίς, ὀστέα. (Il. and Od. 12.85.)

λαυρη.g: λαύρη : lane, side - passage between the house (of Odysseus) and the outer wall of the court, Od. 22.128, 137. (See plate III., o, n.）

λαχεια.g: λάχεια : with good soil for digging, fertile, νῆσος, Od. 9.116 and Od. 10.509.

λαχνη.g: λάχνη : woolly hair, down, Il. 10.134; sparse hair or beard, Il. 2.219, Od. 11.320.

λαω.g: λάω , part. λάων, ipf. λάε: doubtful word, ‘bury the teeth in,’ of a dog strangling a fawn, Od. 19.229 f.

λεβησ.g: λέβης , ητος: kettle, caldron, for warming water or for boiling food over fire, Il. 21.362; in the Odyssey usually, basin, wash-basin, held under the hands or feet while water was poured from a pitcher over them, Od. 19.386; called ἀνθεμόεις, from the decoration, Od. 3.440.

λεγω.g: λέγω , ipf. ἔλεγ̓, λέγε, λέγομεν, fut. part. λέξοντες, aor. ἔλεξεν, imp. λέξον, mid. pres. subj. λεγώμεθα, ipf. λέγοντο, fut. λέξομαι, aor. λέξατο, aor. 2 ἐλέγμην, ἔλεκτο, λέκτο, imp. λέξο, λέξεο, pass. aor. ἐλέχθην. The above forms are common to two distinct roots λεγ, gather, and λεχ, lay. —I. root λεγ, gather, collect, Il. 23.239, Il. 10.755, Od. 18.359, Od. 24.72, 224; count, Od. 4.452; pass., Il. 3.188; then enumerate, recount, tell, relate, Il. 2.222, Od. 5.5, Od. 11.374; mid., collect for oneself, count oneself in, select, Il. 8.507, 547, Od. 9.335, Il. 2.125; λέκτο ἀριθμόν, counted over the number (for himself), Od. 4.451; also talk over (with one another), μηκέτι ταῦτα λεγώμεθα, Od. 3.240.—II. root λεχ, act. aor. 1, lay, put to bed or to rest, Il. 24.635; met., Il. 14.252; mid., fut. and aor. 1 and 2, lay oneself down, lie down to sleep, lie, Od. 4.413, 453, Il. 4.131, Θ 519, Il. 9.67.

λειαινω.g: λειαίνω (λεῖος), fut. λειανέω, aor. 3 pl. λείηναν, part. λειήνα_ς: make smooth, smooth, level off, Od. 8.260.

λειβω.g: λείβω , ipf. λεῖβε, aor. inf. λεῖψαι: pour (in drops), shed, δάκρυα often; also esp., pour a libation, (οἶνον) τινί, or drink-offering; abs., Il. 24.285. (See cut No. 77 on next page; cf. also Nos. 21 and 95.)

λειμων.g: λειμών , ῶνος: meadow, mead; λειμωνόθεν, from the meadow, Il. 24.451.

λειοσ.g: λεῖος (lēvis): smooth, even, level; πετράων, ‘free from rocks,’ Od. 5.443.

λειπω.g: λείπω , ipf. λεῖπ（ε), fut. λείψω, aor. 2 ἔλιπον, λίπον, perf. λέλοιπεν, mid. ipf. λείπετ（ο), aor. 2 λιπόμην, pass. perf. λέλειπται, plup. λελείμμην, fut. perf. λελείψεται, aor. 3 pl. λίπεν: leave, forsake; ἔλιπον ίοί ἄνακτα, arrows ‘failed’ him, Od. 22.119, cf. Od. 14.213; pass. and aor. mid., be left, remain, survive, Il. 12.14; w. gen., be left behind one, as in running, Il. 23.523, 529; λελειμμένος οἰῶν, ‘remaining behind’ the other sheep, Od. 9.448 ; λίπεν ἅρματ᾽ ἀνάκτων, ‘had been forsaken by’ their masters, Il. 16.507.

λειριοεισ.g: λειριόεις , εσσα (λείριον): lily - like, lily-white, Il. 13.830 ; ὄψ, ‘delicate,’ Il. 3.152. (Il.)

λειωδησ.g: Λειώδης : son of Oenops, a suitor of Penelope and the soothsayer of the suitors; he shares their fate, Od. 21.144, Od. 22.310.

λειωκριτοσ.g: Λειώκριτος : (1) son of Arisbas, slain by Aenēas, Il. 17.344.—(2) son of Euēnor, a suitor of Penelope, slain by Telemachus, Od. 2.242, Od. 22.294.

λεκτον.g: Λεκτόν : a promontory on the Trojan coast, opposite Lesbos, Il. 14.284.

λεκτρον.g: λέκτρον (root λεχ): bed, freq. the pl.; λέκτρονδε, Od. 8.292.

λελεγεσ.g: Λέλεγες : a piratical tribe on the south and west coast of Asia Minor, Il. 10.429, Il. 21.86.

λελιημαι.g: λελίημαι : only part., λελιημένος, as adj., eager, desirous; w. ὄφρα, Δ 465, Il. 5.690. Cf. λιλαίομαι. (Il.)

λεοντευσ.g: Λεοντεύς : a Lapith, the son of Corōnus, a suitor of Helen, Il. 2.745, Il. 23.841.

λεπαδνον.g: λέπαδνον , pl. λέπαδνα: breast-collar, a strap passing around the breast of the horses, and made fast to the yoke, Il. 5.730. (See g in cut No. 78 below, also cut No. 45, f.）

λεπτοσ.g: λεπτός (λέπω), sup. λεπτότατος: peeled, husked, Il. 20.497; then thin, fine, narrow, delicate.

λεπω.g: λέπω , aor. ἔλεψεν: peel, strip off; φύλλα, Il. 1.236†.

λεσβοσ.g: Λέσβος : Lesbos, the island opposite the gulf of Adramyttium, Od. 3.169, Il. 24.544 . —Λεσβόθεν, from Lesbos, Il. 9.664 . — Λεσβίς, ίδος: Lesbian woman, Il. 9.129, 271.

λευγαλεοσ.g: λευγαλέος (cf. λυγρός, λοιγός): mournful, miserable.—Adv., λευγαλέως, Il. 13.732.

λευκαινω.g: λευκαίνω : make white, with foam, Od. 12.172†.

λευκασ.g: Λευκάς : πέτρη, ‘White rock,’ at the entrance of the nether world, on the border of Oceanus, Od. 24.11†.

λευκ-ασπισ.g: λεύκ-ασπις , ιδος: with white shield, white-shielded, Il. 22.294†.

λευκοθεη.g: Λευκοθέη : Leucothea, a sea-goddess, once Ino, the daughter of Cadmus, Od. 5.334, 461.

λευκοσ.g: λευκός : clear, i. e. transparent or full of light, as water, the surface of water, or the radiance of the sky, Od. 5.70, Od. 10.94, Od. 6.45; then white, as snow, milk, bones, barley, Il. 10.437, Od. 9.246, Od. 1.161, Il. 20.496.

λευκ - ωλενοσ.g: λευκ - ώλενος (ὠλένη, elbow, forearm): white - armed; epithet of goddesses and women according to the metrical convenience of their names; ἀμφίπολος, δμωαί, ς 198, Od. 19.60.

λευσσω.g: λεύσσω (cf. λευκός, lux), ipf. λεῦσσε: see, behold.

λεχε-ποιησ.g: λεχε-ποίης (λέχος, ποίη): with grassy bed (of a river); grassy (of towns), Il. 4.383, Il. 2.697.

λεχοσ.g: λέχος , εος (root λεχ, λέγω): bed, bedstead, also pl. in both senses; typical in connubial relations, λέχος ἀντιᾶν, πορσύνειν, Α 31, Od. 3.403; funeralcouch, bier, Od. 24.44, Od. 23.165 ; λέχοσδε, to the bed, Il. 3.447.

λεων.g: λέων , οντος, dat. pl. λείουσι and λέουσι: lion; fig., where we should expect ‘lioness,’ Il. 21.483.

ληγω.g: λήγω , inf. ληγέμεναι, ipf. λῆγ̓, fut. λήξω, aor. 3 pl. λῆξαν: leave off, cease, w. gen. or w. part., Il. 6.107, Il. 21.224; trans., abate, μένος, Il. 13.424; χεῖρας φόνοιο, ‘stay’ my hands from slaughter, Od. 22.63.

ληδη.g: Λήδη : Leda, the wife of Tyndareus, mother by Zeus of Helen, Castor, and Polydeuces, and of Clytaemnestra by Tyndareus, Od. 11.298, 300.

ληθανω.g: ληθάνω : cause to forget, τινός, Od. 7.221†.

ληθοσ.g: Λῆθος : son of Teutamus, and father of Hippothous, Il. 2.843, Il. 17.288.

ληι - βοτειρα.g: ληι - βότειρα (λήιον, βόσκω): cropeating, crop-destroying, Od. 18.29†.

ληιζομαι.g: ληίζομαι , fut. ληίσσομαι, aor. ληίσσατο: carry off as booty.

ληιον.g: λήιον : crop, grain still standing in the field, field of grain.

ληιστοσ.g: ληιστός : to be plundered or taken by plundering, see ἑλετός.

ληιτισ.g: ληῖτις , ιδος: booty - bringing, giver of booty, epith. of Athēna, Il. 10.460†.

ληιτοσ.g: Λήιτος : son of Alectryon, a leader of the Boeotians, Il. 2.494, Il. 13.91, Il. 17.601, Il. 6.35.

λημνοσ.g: Λῆμνος : Lemnos, the island west of the Troad, with probably in Homer's time a city of the same name, Il. 14.230, 281; called ἠγαθέη, as sacred to Hephaestus (also to the Cabīri) on account of its volcano, Moschylus; now Stalimene [(ἐ）ς τὴ（ν) Λῆμνον].

λητω.g: Λητώ : Leto (Latona), mother of Apollo and Artemis, Od. 11.580, Il. 1.9; epith., ἐρικυ_δής, ἠύκομος, καλλιπάρῃος.

λιαζομαι.g: λιάζομαι , part. λιαζόμενον, ipf. λιάζετο, aor. pass. (ἐ）λιάσθην: turn aside, withdraw; κῦμα, ‘parted,’ Il. 24.96 ; εἴδωλον, ‘vanished,’ Od. 4.838; also sink down, droop; προτὶ γαίῃ πτερά, Υ 420, Il. 23.879.

λιαροσ.g: λιαρός : warm, lukewarm; αἷμα, ὕδωρ, Λ 477, Od. 24.45; then mild, gentle, Od. 5.268, Il. 14.164.

λιβυη.g: Λιβύη : Libya, west of Egypt, Od. 4.85, Od. 14.295.

λιγα.g: λίγα (λιγύς): adv., clear, loudly, ἀείδειν, κωκύειν.

λιγαινω.g: λιγαίνω (λιγύς): cry with clear, loud voice, Il. 11.685†.

λιγδην.g: λίγδην : adv., grazing; βάλλειν χεῖρα, Od. 22.278†.

λιγυ-πνειων.g: λιγυ-πνείων , οντος: loudly blowing, whistling, Od. 4.567†.

λιγυροσ.g: λιγυρός (λιγύς): clear-toned, whistling, piping; ἀοιδή, μάστιξ, πνοιαί, Od. 12.44, Λ 532, Il. 5.526.

λιγυσ.g: λιγύς , λιγεῖα, λιγύ: clear and loud of tone, said of singers, the harp, an orator, ‘clear-voiced,’ ‘clear-toned,’ Od. 24.62, Il. 9.186, Il. 1.248; of the wind, ‘piping,’ ‘whistling,’ Od. 3.176, Il. 13.334.—Adv., λιγέως, ἀγορεύειν, φυ_σᾶν, κλαίειν, Il. 3.214, Ψ 218, Od. 10.201.

λιγυ-φωνοσ.g: λιγύ-φωνος : with loud, clear note, of a falcon, Il. 19.350†.

λιην.g: λίην : too, excessively, greatly, very; μή τι λίην προκαλίζεο, provoke me not ‘too far,’ Od. 18.20 ; οὐδέ τι λίην οὕτω νώνυμός ἐστι, not so very unrenowned, Od. 13.238, cf. Od. 15.405; often καὶ λίην at the beginning of a statement, ‘most certainly,’ ‘ay, by all means,’ etc.

λιθασ.g: λιθάς , άδος, dat. pl. λιθάδεσσι = λίθος. (Od.)

λιθοσ.g: λίθος , usually m.: stone, rock; fig. as symbol of firmness, or of harshness, Od. 19.494, Il. 4.510.

λικμαω.g: λικμάω (λικμός), part. gen. plur. λικμώντων: winnow, Il. 5.500†.

λικμητηρ.g: λικμητήρ , ῆρος: winnower, who threw the grain with his winnowingshovel against the wind, thus separating it from the chaff, Il. 13.590†.

λικριφισ.g: λικριφίς : adv., sideways, to one side, Il. 14.463 and Od. 19.451.

λικυμνιοσ.g: Λικύμνιος : brother of Alcmēna, slain by Tlepolemus, Il. 2.663†.

λιλαια.g: Λίλαια : a town in Phocis, at the source of the Cephissus, Il. 2.523†.

λιλαιομαι.g: λιλαίομαι , ipf. λιλαίετο: desire, be desirous of or eager for, τινός, Od. 13.31; freq. w. inf.; with the inf. omitted, Od. 11.223; metaph., of the lance, λιλαιομένη χροὸς ἆσαι. Cf. λελίημαι.

λιμην.g: λιμήν , ένος (cf. λείβω, λίμνη): harbor; pl. also in signif. of inlets, bays, Il. 23.745, Od. 13.96, Od. 4.846.

λιμνη.g: λίμνη (cf. λείβω, λιμήν): lake, pond, even of a swamp or a marsh, Il. 21.317; also of the sea, Od. 3.1.

λινδοσ.g: Λίνδος : a town in Rhodes. Il. 2.656†.

λινο - θωρηξ.g: λινο - θώρηξ : with linen cuirass, Il. 2.529. (As represented in adjoining cut, No. 79; cf. also No. 12.)

λινον.g: λίνον : flax, then anything made of it, thread, yarn, esp. fishing - line, Il. 16.408; of a fisher's net, Il. 5.487; linen cloth, linen, Il. 9.681; fig., of the thread of destiny, Il. 20.128, Il. 24.210, Od. 7.198. (See cuts under ἠλακάτη.)

λινοσ.g: λίνος : lay of Linus, the Linus-song, an ancient popular melody, Il. 18.570†.

λιπα.g: λίπα : adv., always λίπ᾽ ἐλαίῳ, richly with olive oil; but if the word is really an old dat., then with olive oil, ἐλαίῳ being adj.

λιπαρο - κρηδεμνοσ.g: λιπαρο - κρήδεμνος : with shining head-band, Il. 18.382†.

λιπαρο - πλοκαμοσ.g: λιπαρο - πλόκαμος : with shining locks or braids, Il. 19.126†.

λιπαροσ.g: λιπαρός (λίπα): sleek, shining with ointment, Od. 15.332; shining (nitidus), Il. 2.44; then fig., rich, comfortable, θέμιστες, γῆρας, Ι 156, Od. 11.136.—Adv., λιπαρῶς, fig., Od. 4.210.

λιποω.g: λιπόω : be sleek, v. l., Od. 19.72†.

λισσομαι.g: λίσσομαι (λιτή), ipf. (ἐ)(λ）λίσσετο, iter. λισσέσκετο, aor. 1 ἐλλισάμην, imp. λίσαι, aor. 2 ἐλιτόμην, inf. λιτέσθαι: pray, beseech with prayer; abs., Il. 22.91, Od. 2.68, and τινὰ εὐχῇσι, εὐχωλῇσι λιτῆσί τε, Ζηνός, ‘in the name of Zeus’; πρός, ὑπέρ τινος, γούνων (λαβών, ἁψάμενος), etc.; foll. by inf., sometimes ὅπως or ἵνα, Od. 3.19, 237, Od. 8.344; with two accusatives, Od. 2.210, cf. Od. 4.347.

λιστρον.g: λίστρον : hoe or scraper, used in cleaning the floor of a hall, Od. 22.455†.

λιτανευω.g: λιτανεύω (λιτή), ipf. ἐλλιτάνευε, λιτάνευε, fut. λιτανεύσομεν, aor. ἐλλιτάνευσα: pray, implore, abs., and w. acc., Od. 7.145, Il. 9.581.

λοβοσ.g: λοβός : lobe of the ear, pl. Il. 14.182†.

λογοσ.g: λόγος (λέγω): tale, story, as entertaining recital, with enumeration of details, pl., Il. 15.393 and Od. 1.56.

λοετρον.g: λοετρόν (λοϝετρόν, λούω): bathing, bath, pl., Ὠκεανοι῀ο, ‘in Ocean,’ Od. 5.275.

λοετρο - χοοσ.g: λοετρο - χοός (χέω): pouring (containing) water for the bath, τρίπος, tripod with water - kettle, Il. 18.346, Od. 8.435; subst., bath-maid, Od. 20.297.

λοιγιοσ.g: λοίγιος (λοιγός): destructive, ruinous, deadly; as subst., Il. 21.533, Il. 23.310. (Il.)

λοιγοσ.g: λοιγός : destruction, ruin, death, by sickness (pestilence) or war. (Il.)

λοισθηιοσ.g: λοισθήιος (λοῖσθος): for the last in the race, only of prizes, ἄεθλον; and as subst. λοισθήια (cf. πρωτεῖα, δευτερεῖα), prize for the last, Il. 23.751. (Il.)

λοκροι.g: Λοκροί : the Locrians, a tribe occupying one of the divisions of Hellas, and dwelling on the Eurīpus, on both sides of Mt. Cnemis, Il. 2.527, 535, Il. 13.686.

λουω, λοεω.g: λούω, λοέω (cf. lavo), ipf. λοῦον, λὄ (λόϝε), aor. λοῦς（εν), subj. λούσῃ, imp. λόεσον, λούσατε, inf. λοέ（ς）σαι, part. λοέσα_σα, mid. pres. inf. λούεσθαι, λοῦσθαι, fut. λοέσσομαι, aor. λοέσσατο, λούσαντο, etc., pass. perf. part. λελουμένος: bathe, wash, mid., bathe, get washed. Il. 6.508; fig., of the rising of Sirius, λελουμένος Ὠκεανοῖο, ‘after his bath in Ocean,’ Il. 5.6.

λοφιη.g: λοφιή (λόφος): the bristly ridge or comb of a wild boar's back, Od. 19.446†.

λοφοσ.g: λόφος : (1) crest or plume of a helmet, usually of horse - hair, Il. 5.743. (See adjoining cuts, and Nos. 3, 11, 12, 16, 17, 35, 73, 116, 122.)—(2) back of the neck of animals or of men, Il. 23.508, Il. 10.573.—(3) hill, ridge. (Od.)

λοχαω.g: λοχάω (λόχος), aor. inf. λοχῆσαι, mid. fut. λοχήσομαι, aor. part. λοχησάμενος: act. and mid., lie in ambush, lie in wait for, waylay, τινά, Od. 13.425.

λοχμη.g: λόχμη (root λεχ): lair of a wild beast, thicket, jungle, Od. 19.439†.

λοχοσ.g: λόχος (root λεχ): place of ambush, act of lying in wait; said of the Trojan horse, Il. 18.513, Od. 4.277; also of the party forming the ambuscade, Il. 8.522; and of any armed company, Od. 20.49 ; λόχος γέροντος, ‘means of entrapping’ the old man of the sea, Od. 4.395 .— λόχονδε: upon an ambuscade, into the ambush, Il. 1.227, Od. 14.217.

λυγροσ.g: λυγρός (cf. λευγαλέος): sad, mournful, miserable; in apparently active sense, φάρμακα, σήματα, etc., Od. 4.230, Il. 6.168; also fig., and in derogatory sense, ‘sorry,’ εἵματα, Od. 16.457; so of persons, Il. 13.119.—Adv., λυγρῶς.

λυθρον.g: λύθρον : properly pollution, then gore (or blood mixed with dust), with and without αἷμα.

λυκα - βα_σ.g: λυκά - βα_ς , αντος (root λυκ, lux, βαίνω): year, Od. 14.161 and Od. 19.306.

λυκαστοσ.g: Λύκαστος : a town in the southern part of Crete, Il. 2.647.

λυκαων.g: Λυκάων : (1) a Lycian, the father of Pandarus, Il. 5.197, 95.—(2) son of Priam and Laothoe, slain by Achilles, Il. 21.144 ff.

λυκη - γενησ.g: λυκη - γενής , έος (root λυκ, lux): light-born, epith. of Apollo as sun-god, Il. 4.101, 119.

λυκιη.g: Λυκίη : Lycia.—(1) a division of Asia Minor, Il. 2.877.—(2) a district on the river Aesēpus, its chief town Zeleia, Il. 2.824, Il. 5.173 .—Λυκίηθεν, from Lycia, Il. 5.105 .—Λυκίηνδε, to Lycia, Il. 6.168.

λυκιοι.g: Λύκιοι : the Lycians, inhabitants of Lycia (1). Led by Glaucus and by Sarpēdon, Il. 7.13, Il. 5.647, Il. 14.426, Il. 16.490.

λυκομηδησ.g: Λυκομήδης : son of Creon in Boeotia, Il. 17.346, Il. 19.240.

λυκοοργοσ.g: Λυκόοργος (Λυκοϝ.): Lycurgus.— (1) son of Dryas, king of the Edonians in Thrace, banishes from his land the worship of Dionȳsus (Bacchus), Il. 6.134. —(2) an Arcadian, slays Arithous, Il. 7.142-148.

λυκοσ.g: λύκος (ϝλύκος): wolf; symbol of bloodthirstiness, Il. 4.471, Il. 11.72.

λυκοφοντησ.g: Λυκοφόντης : a Trojan, slain by Teucer, Il. 8.275.

λυκοφρων.g: Λυκόφρων : son of Mastor, from Cythēra, a companion of Ajax, Il. 15.430.

λυκτοσ.g: Λύκτος : a city in Crete, east of Cnosus, Il. 2.647, Il. 17.611.

λυκων.g: Λύκων : a Trojan, slain by Peneleüs, Il. 16.335, 337.

λυμα.g: λῦμα , pl. λύματα: anything washed away, defilement, Il. 14.171; in symbolical and ritualistic sense, offerings of purification, Il. 1.314.

λυρνη（σ）σοσ.g: Λυρνη（ς）σός : Lyrnessus, a town in Mysia, under the sway of Hypoplacian Thebes, Il. 2.690, Il. 19.60, Il. 20.92, 191.

λυσανδροσ.g: Λύσανδρος : a Trojan, slain by Ajax, Il. 11.491†.

λυ_σι-μελησ.g: λυ_σι-μελής , ές (λύω, μέλος): relaxing the limbs, ὕπνος, Od. 20.57 (with a play upon the word in v. 56).

λυσισ.g: λύσις , ιος (λύω): loosing, ransoming, Il. 24.655 ; θανάτου, ‘deliverance’ from death, Od. 9.421.

λυσσητηρ.g: λυσσητήρ , ῆρος: one who rages, raging, w. κύων, Il. 8.299†.

λυω.g: λύω , ipf. ἔλυον, λύε, fut. λύσω, aor. ἔλυ_σα, λῦσεν, mid. aor. ἐλύσαο, inf. λύσασθαι, aor. 2, w. pass. signif., λύτο, λύντο, pass. perf. λέλυμαι, opt. λελῦτο, aor. λύθη, 3 pl. λύθεν: I. act., loose, loosen, set free, of undoing garments, ropes, Il. 4.215, Od. 11.245, Od. 2.415; unharnessing horses, Od. 4.35; of freeing from bonds or captivity (said of the captor), Il. 1.20; pass., of anything giving way, coming apart, Il. 2.135, Od. 22.186; fig., in senses answering to those enumerated, τινὰ κακότητος, ‘deliver’ from misery; ἀγορήν, ‘dismiss’; so λύτο δ᾽ ἀγών; and with reference to emotion, or fainting, death, λύτο γούνατα καὶ φίλον ἦτορ, ‘gave way,’ ‘sank,’ ‘quaked’ (sometimes the act., Od. 20.118); of sleep ‘relaxing’ the limbs, or ‘dissolving’ cares, Od. 4.794, Il. 23.62; of ‘undoing’ (destroying) cities, Il. 2.118.—III. mid., loose or undo oneself, Od. 9.463, or something of one's own, get loosed or released, ransom; λυ_σόμενος θύγατρα, said of the father, Il. 1.13; cf. the act., v. 20.

λωβαομαι.g: λωβάομαι (λώβη), aor. imp. λωβήσασθε, opt. λωβήσαιο: maltreat, outrage; w. cognate acc. and obj. τινὰ λώβην, do despite, Il. 13.623.

λωβη.g: λώβη : outrage, insult; σοὶ λώβη, ‘shame upon thee,’ if, etc., Il. 18.180; of a person, ‘object of ignominy,’ Il. 3.42.

λωβητηρ.g: λωβητήρ , ῆρος: one who outrages or insults, slanderer, scoundrel, Il. 2.275, Il. 11.385. (Il.)

λωιον, λωιτερον.g: λώϊον, λωΐτερον: better, preferable; ‘more liberally,’ Od. 17.417.

λωτουντα.g: λωτοῦντα (λωτός), either a part., or adj., for λωτόεντα: full of lotus, ‘clovery,’ πεδία, Il. 12.283†.

λωτοσ.g: λωτός : lotus.—(1) a species of clover, Od. 4.603, Il. 14.348.—(2) the tree and fruit enjoyed by the Lotus-eaters, Od. 9.91 ff. Said to be a plant with fruit the size of olives, in taste resembling dates, still prized in Tunis and Tripoli under the name of Jujube.

λωφαω.g: λωφάω , fut. λωφήσει, aor. opt. λωφήσειε: rest from, cease from, retire, Od. 9.460, Il. 21.292.
